query: What travel policy risks appear in expense descriptions?

per_column.name: asset_category_type
per_column.rationale: Describes what kind of asset/item the expense is for. This is a contextual attribute that may predict risk but is not itself an aspect of travel policy risk.

per_column.name: travel_equipment_marker
per_column.rationale: Flags whether the item is travel equipment; identifies subject matter relevance, not a constitutive dimension of the risk itself.

per_column.name: expense_automation_method
per_column.rationale: How the expense entry was generated (automatic vs manual) is a process attribute, not a part of policy risk. At best a weak predictor of control weakness.

per_column.name: receipt_or_approval_risk
per_column.rationale: Receipt/approval/pre-approval requirements are a genuine documentation-and-authorization facet of travel policy compliance risk.

per_column.name: personal_use_risk_indicator
per_column.rationale: Personal (non-business) use is a legitimate constitutive dimension of travel policy risk (misuse/ineligibility).

per_column.name: department_compliance_context
per_column.rationale: Owning department is a segmentation/context attribute of the expense, not an aspect of the risk concept itself.

per_column.name: ci_vendor_brand
per_column.rationale: Vendor/brand of the configuration item is descriptive metadata unrelated to constituting policy risk.

per_column.name: high_value_risk_flag
per_column.rationale: Excess/high monetary value relative to policy limits is a genuine spend-threshold facet of travel policy risk.

per_column.name: miscellaneous_or_undefined_asset
per_column.rationale: Whether the asset is uncategorized is a data-quality/classification attribute, at best a predictor, not a facet of the risk.

judge.rationale: Only three of nine columns are constitutive facets of travel_policy_risk: documentation/approval requirements, personal-use misuse, and high-value/limit breach. The remaining six are external predictors or irrelevant metadata (asset type, travel markers, entry method, department, vendor brand, data-completeness), which describe the expense context rather than parts of the risk concept. Among the genuine facets, exclusivity is fairly good (documentation vs personal-use vs monetary-threshold are distinct), lowered slightly by overlapping generic 'risk' framing. Exhaustiveness is weak: important constitutive facets of travel policy risk—such as booking-timing/advance-purchase compliance, allowable-class/rate limits, out-of-policy category (e.g., alcohol/entertainment), duplicate/split claims, and geographic/per-diem limits—are not covered.
